title: In the Absence of Knowledge
subtitle: Cache geometry separates real-entity from fake-entity prompts (encoding-only equivalence unverified); the hedging-style choice is a coin flip at a balanced logit
abstract: KV-cache geometry separates real-entity from fake-entity prompts (a canonical template referent against a minor place name or category error; none of the fake entities is fabricated, the model answers several, and ten of 15 end in -ton) at AUROC 0.9288, a bootstrap mean ([0.8192, 0.9886], not clustered by prompt pair; no text baseline or template-held-out test has been run) (encoding-only: 0.9377 [0.8356, 0.9941], unverified: BLOCKER-1) on token-matched prompts. If that unverified figure holds, encoding-only features achieve equivalent separation to the full classifier --- generation-phase features add no measurable discriminative power. The model generates more confident tokens on fake-entity prompts than on real ones (logit margin d=0.91). The hedge/confab decision resolves at a single balanced-logit token where sampling determines framing, not truthfulness. On 45 unanswerable questions (responses capped at 80 tokens) a three-judge panel puts the confab rate at 13.3% (per judge 8.9-15.6%; a single 3B judge, 3/45), not the 73% of regex classifiers.
